rationale: PINS that a type-only import edge says so. `import type { T } from 'm'` is ERASED by the compiler, so it is a type dependency and not a runtime one. Measured on element-plus, 400 admitted files, production parseFile: 655 `import_statement` nodes carry the `type` modifier across 279 files; 982 type-only specifiers against 2,058 value specifiers, i.e. 32% of the import surface. All 271 files with a type-only import already emitted an `imports` edge, and 0 of those edges carried any type-only marker, so the graph asserted a runtime dependency the compiler denies and a consumer could not tell the two apart. The `forbid` entries are the half that carries the meaning: an analyzer that set the marker unconditionally would assert every import is erased, which is the opposite error.
